Since genealogies were very important in ancient Israel, how is it that Lehi did not know his tribal affiliation until reading the record on the brass plates of Laban (1 Nephi 5:14)? It was the extended family, not the tribe, that was the most important family unit in ancient Israel. More important, there is evidence from the Bible itself that people were not totally aware of their genealogy (Ezra 2:62; Nehemiah 7:64). For instance, we do not know the tribal affiliation of Elijah, one of the more important prophets in the Bible. Since Lehi's ancestors would have come to the Kingdom of Judah as immigrants from the Kingdom of Israel (he did, after all, live in Jerusalem) they may not have wished to flaunt their origins and later generations may have come to assume that they were of Judah, Benjamin, Levi, or Simeon.
